Best Things to Do in Raleigh this Weekend + (Nov 9 – Nov 15, 2026)

By Caroline Makepeace | November 9, 2026 | This post may contain affiliate links. We may receive a small commission, at no cost to you, if you make a purchase. Read Disclosure
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 26:45
Instaread

We had a lot of fun this weekend perusing local art at the Falls Art Fair, eating lots of yummy oysters at the Oysterfest, and eating Raleigh’s best hamburger finally, at Lagana’s and learned why their burgers are so raveable! (Be sure to subscribe to our newsletter as we share all the finds like this!)

If you’d like to do some good this month too, our Feed the Pack Pantry Bowl guide shows how a $5 gift to NC State’s food pantry counts in the Pantry Bowl rivalry with UNC through Nov 30. We love sharing this annual Fall event to help support our local scholars!

Speaking of this rivalry, the UNC and NC State men’s soccer team will meet on the pitch in Cary this Thursday in the ACC tournament semi-finals! Which means we’ll have one Triangle team in the finals on Sunday! And for the women, another rivalry match will happen on Thursday, Duke vs. UNC, also in Cary! Again, at least one Triangle women’s team will be in the final on Sunday!

Candlelight concerts return to The Rialto on Friday and Saturday, and Death Becomes Her plays DPAC every night from Tuesday through Sunday. Vintage Market Days takes over the NC State Fairgrounds from Friday to Sunday, so there is room for a bit of holiday shopping in between.

We update this post every Monday with the week’s events in Raleigh. We cover a wide range of interests and add ideas that aren’t event based, like a museum visit or a hike. We check the details for every event, but please do your own due diligence before you go. Make sure it hasn’t sold out, been cancelled or changed, and check current prices.

P.S. Please share this post with your Raleigh friends to help them plan their week too! Sign up for our email newsletter here.

Skip to What’s Happening today in Raleigh

It’s possible you landed here on a Friday or Saturday, and so what happened on Monday is of no concern to you. if you just want to know what is happening today in Raleigh, then click the links below to jump down to the today in Raleigh you are most interested in!

  • Today in Raleigh on a Monday
  • Today in Raleigh Tuesday
  • Today in Raleigh on a Wednesday
  • Today in Raleigh Thursday
  • Today in Raleigh on a Friday
  • Today in Raleigh on Saturday
  • Today in Raleigh on Sunday

Happening all week in Raleigh

Big events

These events run every day (or most days) of this week, so we’ve listed them once instead of repeating them under each day.

  • Death Becomes Her The Broadway musical plays DPAC in Durham Tuesday through Sunday, with 7:30pm shows Tuesday to Friday, 2pm and 7:30pm on Saturday, and 1pm and 6:30pm on Sunday. Tickets start at $55.
  • Vintage Market Days: A Vintage Noel A three-day holiday market at the NC State Fairgrounds, 4285 Trinity Rd, Friday and Saturday 10am to 5pm and Sunday 10am to 4pm. Kids under 12 are free.
  • Skate the Square at Fenton The outdoor ice rink at Fenton in Cary is open for the season, and we have the details in our November events in Raleigh guide.

Ghost tours, exhibitions, and games

  • Rust, Rebels & Ruins Ghost Tour One of our favorite ghost tours in downtown Raleigh. A lantern-led walk past eight historic spots, starting at the NC State Capitol. From $26.
  • Raleigh Haunted Footsteps Ghost Tour A guided ghost walk through downtown Raleigh.
  • Sip & Stroll Raleigh Ghost Tour About 1 hour 10 minutes through downtown’s haunted spots. Starts at Exchange Place, next to the Poyner YMCA. Pay what you wish, usually $15 to $20 per adult.
  • Spirits and Spirits Haunted Cocktail Rydables Tour Glide around downtown on a plush Rydable, sipping cocktails and hearing Raleigh’s eerie legends. About 2 hours, meets at 400 Fayetteville St. $95.
  • Ghosts of Raleigh: Explore the Haunted Past! A self-guided outdoor ghost hunt using your phone as a detector, across haunted downtown spots.
  • Raleigh Murder Mystery: Solve the Case! A self-guided outdoor game, this one a whodunit downtown.
  • Detective Mystery Game (Cary version) The same idea, set in Cary.
  • Kid Quest in Raleigh A self-guided scavenger hunt for families with kids ages 4 to 8, starting at 520 Ashe Ave. Play any day, about 60 minutes, from $8.
  • Dorothy’s Quest: The Trials of Oz from Nash Square or Raleigh’s Secret Society Self-guided games for older kids and adults.
  • Pumpkin season is still going. Our pumpkin patches guide covers patches, corn mazes and hayrides near Raleigh.
  • Raleigh Murder Mystery 2: Crime on Date Night A newer self-guided detective game built for two, starting from Exchange Plaza downtown. Start any day, any time (evenings are best).

What’s happening this week in Raleigh

Monday, Nov 9, 2026

Monday is light on events, so it is a good night for one of the ghost tours or self-guided games in the Happening all week section above.

Tuesday, Nov 10, 2026

  • Lake Lynn Loop Trail Kick-off A guided kick-off for the Lake Lynn Loop trail at Lake Lynn Park, 7921 Ray Rd, 10am to 11am. FREE and open to all ages.
  • Join Us as We Honor Raleigh’s Veterans A Veterans Day program at John Chavis Community Center, 505 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, 11am to 1pm. FREE for veterans and $5 for guests, and registration is required.
  • Modi and Hunter Luke Edwards, Goodnights Comedy Club. Modi is listed as sold out.
  • Switchfoot with Anberlin, The Ritz.
  • NC State Men’s Basketball vs. Presbyterian Lenovo Center
  • Roots of Discovery: Festival of Lights: Experience the vibrant traditions of India and explore the connections between cultural heritage, science and the natural world. NC Museum of Natural Sciences 10:30am – 1pm Free

Wednesday, Nov 11, 2026 (Veteren’s Day)

  • Apex Veterans Day Ceremony Apex American Legion Post 124 hosts the ceremony at the Downtown Service Memorial, Saunders St and N Salem St, 9:30am to 10:30am. FREE. If it rains it moves to Apex Fire Station 1.
  • Holly Springs Veterans Day Ceremony At the Veterans Memorial at Veterans Park, 600 Bikram Dr, 11am. FREE.
  • O Brother, Where Art Thou? The Coen brothers film on the big screen at The Rialto, 1620 Glenwood Ave. Doors 6:30pm, show 7pm, $11.
  • Will Burkart and Francisco Ramos, Goodnights Comedy Club. Will Burkart is listed as sold out, and Francisco Ramos performs in Spanish on Wednesday.
  • Slaughter To Prevail, The Ritz.
  • Free Yoga Class with Canned Food Donation benefiting the local food bank 7pm – 8pm 621 Hillsborough St

Thursday, Nov 12, 2026

  • ACC Men’s Soccer Championship semifinals Two semifinal matches at First Horizon Stadium at WakeMed Soccer Park, NC State will play UNC at 5:30pm and Syracuse vs SMU at 8:30pm 201 Soccer Park Dr in Cary, at 5:30pm and 8:30pm. Ticketed – one price gets you in for the men’s and women’s games!
  • ACC Women’s Soccer Championship semifinals Two semifinal matches at First Horizon Stadium at WakeMed Soccer Park, #6 Duke vs. #2 North Carolina | 2 p.m. | & 5 Virginia vs. 1 Notre Dame at 11am 201 Soccer Park Dr in Cary, Ticketed.
  • Carolina Hurricanes vs Seattle Kraken The first of two NHL Global Series games in Helsinki, Finland, at 12pm ET. It is not a Lenovo Center game.
  • Five Points Short Film Festival A night of short films at The Rialto, 1620 Glenwood Ave. Doors 6:15pm, show 7pm, $27.50 to $33.
  • Francisco Ramos and Emma Willmann, Goodnights Comedy Club.
  • The Elovaters, The Ritz.
  • Through Her Voice at Little Native Co Four featured women poets each choose two poems from DS Will’s book, read them, and share what the poems mean to them and why they chose them. 6pm – 8pm $10
  • Longleaf Picture Show: Moonrise Kingdom Longleaf Hotel patio 6:30pm – 8:30pm FREE

Friday, Nov 13, 2026

  • Moonlight in the Garden The second of three weekends at the JC Raulston Arboretum, 4415 Beryl Rd. It is an after-dark evening in the garden and it is ticketed.
  • Candlelight: Coldplay and Imagine Dragons and Candlelight: 90s Hip-Hop on Strings Candlelight concerts at The Rialto, 1620 Glenwood Ave, at 5:30pm and 7:45pm.
  • Carolina Youth Ballet: The Nutcracker Fletcher Opera Theater at Martin Marietta Center, 6pm.
  • NC Symphony: How to Train Your Dragon in Concert The film plays on screen while the symphony performs the score live, Meymandi Concert Hall at Martin Marietta Center, 7:30pm.
  • A Magical Cirque Christmas A holiday cirque show at Memorial Auditorium at Martin Marietta Center, 8pm.
  • Apex Community Dance A family-friendly square, English country and contra dance with local callers and live musicians, at The Halle Cultural Arts Center, 237 N Salem St in Apex, 7pm to 9pm. No experience needed and tickets are $2.
  • Fuquay Film Festival Two days of short films at the Fuquay-Varina Arts Center, Friday and Saturday.
  • Broken Compass Bluegrass, Garner Performing Arts Center, 7:30pm.
  • An Evening With Shadowgrass, Lincoln Theatre, doors 7:30pm and show 8:30pm.
  • Level Up, The Ritz.
  • NC State Men’s Basketball vs. Troy, Lenovo Center
  • Emma Willmann, Goodnights Comedy Club

Saturday, Nov 14, 2026

  • Hot Dogs with Heroes An autism awareness event with Raleigh Fire at Fire Station 12, 4306 Poole Rd, 11am to 1pm. FREE, and registration is required through Eventbrite with one ticket per family.
  • NC State vs Syracuse, Carter-Finley Stadium.
  • Forest Park Art Walk 2026 This free, self-guided event invites art lovers, neighbors, families, and holiday shoppers to explore the studios and creative spaces of artists throughout this walkable, tree-lined neighborhood near downtown Raleigh.  1- 5pm
  • Quail Hollow ARTWalk 2026 Visit neighborhood artists displaying and selling their artwork on porches, sidewalks, yards, etc., in the Quail Hollow area of Raleigh. 10am – 2pm
  • Carolina Hurricanes vs Seattle Kraken The second Helsinki game, at 1pm ET.
  • NCMA Movies at Moore Square: Wicked: For Good (2025) at Moore Square 3pm
  • Carolina Youth Ballet: The Nutcracker Fletcher Opera Theater at Martin Marietta Center, 12pm and 3:30pm.
  • NC Symphony: How to Train Your Dragon in Concert Meymandi Concert Hall at Martin Marietta Center, 3pm.
  • Moonlight in the Garden The second Saturday night at the JC Raulston Arboretum. Ticketed.
  • Candlelight: Neo-Soul Favorites and Candlelight: Tribute to Fleetwood Mac Candlelight concerts at The Rialto, 1620 Glenwood Ave, at 5:30pm and 7:45pm.
  • The Jury Experience: The Deadly Boat Ride A show at Jones Auditorium at Meredith College, 4:30pm and 7pm, from $48.
  • Art Bash Artspace’s 40th anniversary fundraiser at 201 E Davie St, from 6pm. General admission is $175, and an after-party only ticket is $25.
  • Fuquay Film Festival Day two at the Fuquay-Varina Arts Center.
  • Southern Shade of Blue: Carrie Marshall, Garner Performing Arts Center, 7:30pm.
  • PLUS Dueling Pianos Road Show, Lincoln Theatre, doors 7pm and show 8pm, $24.25 to $37.75.
  • Orville Peck, The Ritz.
  • Emma Willmann, Goodnights Comedy Club.

Sunday, Nov 15, 2026

  • ACC Men’s Soccer Championship final The championship match at First Horizon Stadium at WakeMed Soccer Park, 201 Soccer Park Dr in Cary, at 4pm. Ticketed. One price gets you to see the men’s and women’s final.
  • ACC Women’s Soccer Championship final The championship match at First Horizon Stadium at WakeMed Soccer Park, 201 Soccer Park Dr in Cary, at 12pm. Ticketed.
  • Jewish History Trolley Tour at Mordecai Historic Park.  a guided trolley tour exploring the people, places, and stories that shaped the city’s Jewish community $15 1- 4pm
  • Forest Park Art Walk 2026 This free, self-guided event invites art lovers, neighbors, families, and holiday shoppers to explore the studios and creative spaces of artists throughout this walkable, tree-lined neighborhood near downtown Raleigh.  1- 5pm
  • Seonghum Jeong: Paderewski Piano Festival A piano recital in the SECU Auditorium at the North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, 3pm, $31.
  • Classical Concert Series: A World in Three Voices Music for violin, trumpet and piano at The Halle Cultural Arts Center, 237 N Salem St in Apex, 3pm to 4pm. Tickets are $18 for adults, $15 for seniors and $12 for ages 16 and under.
  • ELVIS: In Person, starring Matt Stone, Fletcher Opera Theater at Martin Marietta Center, 7pm.

Plan in Advance

Here we like to share things events coming soon in Raleigh to help you book a ticket before they sell out. Or to make sure you get it in your calendar.

  • Nov 20 to 21: Moonlight in the Garden at JC Raulston Arboretum
  • Nov 14: Candlelight: Tribute to Fleetwood Mac at The Rialto See our guide to Candlelight concerts in Raleigh
  • Nov 21 to Jan 10: North Carolina Chinese Lantern Festival at Koka Booth Amphitheatre in Cary, open daily 6pm to 10pm except Christmas Day, tickets on sale
  • Dec 5: Cary Ballet’s Nutcracker at Martin Marietta Center.
  • Dec 7: Pentatonix, Christmas in the City at Lenovo Center
  • Dec 10: Trans-Siberian Orchestra, The Ghosts of Christmas Eve at Lenovo Center
  • Dec 10 to 24: Carolina Ballet’s The Nutcracker at Martin Marietta Center
  • Dec 16 to 20: Disney On Ice: Spotlight Magic at Lenovo Center
  • December: Great Raleigh Trolley Santa Express, where several December evening departures are already sold out or nearly full
  • More December picks are in our December events in Raleigh guide.
  • More Candlelight concerts are on the calendar in Raleigh. See our guide to Candlelight concerts in Raleigh.

Common Questions about Events in Raleigh for the week

What’s the best free thing to do in Raleigh this weekend?

Hot Dogs with Heroes at Fire Station 12 in Raleigh on Saturday is one of the best free things to do in Raleigh this weekend, and the Veterans Day ceremonies in Apex and Holly Springs on Wednesday are free too.

What’s happening in Raleigh this Saturday night?

On Saturday night in Raleigh, Candlelight: Tribute to Fleetwood Mac plays The Rialto at 7:45pm, PLUS Dueling Pianos is at Lincoln Theatre at 8pm, Orville Peck is at The Ritz, and Art Bash is at Artspace from 6pm.

Are there any family-friendly events in Raleigh this weekend?

Family-friendly events in Raleigh this weekend include Vintage Market Days at the NC State Fairgrounds, where kids under 12 are free, Carolina Youth Ballet’s The Nutcracker at Martin Marietta Center on Saturday, and Hot Dogs with Heroes at Fire Station 12.

What outdoor events are happening in Raleigh this weekend?

Outdoor events in Raleigh this weekend include Moonlight in the Garden at the JC Raulston Arboretum, NC State vs Syracuse at Carter-Finley Stadium on Saturday, and the ACC Men’s Soccer Championship final at WakeMed Soccer Park in Cary on Sunday.

What’s the one event in Raleigh this weekend you shouldn’t miss?

Moonlight in the Garden at the JC Raulston Arboretum is the event not to miss this week in Raleigh, and NC State vs Syracuse at Carter-Finley Stadium on Saturday is the sports pick.

  • A Guide to WakeMed Soccer Park: Home to North Carolina FC and NC Courage
  • Guide To Reynolds Coliseum (NC State University’s Iconic Venue: Home to Wolfpack Women’s Basketball
  • Guide To Carter-Finley Stadium: Home Of NC State Football
  • A Guide to Candlelight concerts in Raleigh
  • The North Carolina Museum of Art guide

  • A guide to Red Hat Amphitheater (outdoor venue)
  • A guide to Coastal Credit Union Music Park (outdoor venue)
  • A guide to the Ritz (indoor venue)

RALEIGH TOURS TO CONSIDER

  • If you like walking tours, this Rust, Rebels, & Ruins may be a hit for couples who love to get their SPOOK on. Uncover the lurking ghosts and spirits of Raleigh on a guided paranormal walking tour. Stand as close as you dare to the Heck-Andrews House and listen to chilling tales of this city’s dark history. See our review of this fun ghost tour in Raleigh.
  • Oakwood and N. Blount Architecture & History Tour: Explore the historic streets of Oakwood and North Blount, featuring many of Raleigh’s most breathtaking historic homes.
  • Tour the Joel Lane House Weds-Fri weekly; 10am, 11am, 12pm, and 1pm & Sat 1pm, 2pm, & 3pm. $4-$8 Explore the beginnings of Raleigh, Wake County, North Carolina, and the United States—from the colonial era, through the Revolutionary War, into the first years of a new nation at the oldest house in Raleigh.
  • Raleigh Downtown: Historic Walking Tours: This walking tour takes you between some of Raleigh’s historic downtown sites, including the Heck-Andrews House, Christ Church, Haywood Hall, and much, much more.
  • Raleigh African American History Tour: The tour will take you between various historic sites created by or important to Raleigh’s African American community. Has produced educators, engineers, political leaders, medical scientists, military officers, and much more.
  • Burgers, Brews & Views Bike tour in Johnston County with Triangle Adventures.
  • Ghosts, Mysteries and History ebike tour along the Art to Heart trail.
  • Raleigh Rydables Tour: Landmarks, Legends & Hidden Gems: Explore Raleigh’s landmarks and vibrant districts on a guided Rydable tour. Discover hidden gems, learn about the city’s history, and stop for photos at iconic landmarks.
  • Trolley Pub Public Tour of Raleigh – Grab your friends and dive into Raleigh’s vibrant scene with our two-hour pedal-powered pub adventure! Bring your own drinks Fri – Sun various times.

ENJOY THESE GARDENS FOR A STROLL

Time to soak up those colors and smells at the following Triangle gardens and parks.

  • Sarah P Duke Gardens in Durham are stunning!
  • JC Raulston Arboretum at NC State
  • The Raleigh Rose garden
  • Here are more lovely gardens in Raleigh
  • Dorothea Dix Park has lots of spots for picnics … views included.
  • Juniper Level Botanic Gardens
  • WRAL Azalea Gardens

WANT TO GO FOR A HIKE?

Any day is a good day for a hike. Below are a few of our favorite trails in Raleigh. All of these are great for kids too:

  • FOR LAKE VIEWS: The easy 3-mile paved loop around Lake Johnson
  • FOR A FOREST IMMERSION: Loblolly Trail, Umstead State Park
  • FOR UNIQUENESS: Hemlock Bluffs in Cary
  • ART, NATURE & CITY: Enjoy this ultimate combo on the 6-mile one way Art to Heart bike trail
  • FOR A LONGER UMSTEAD HIKE: Company Mill Trail in Umstead State Park

If these ideas don’t warm up your heart, choose one from this list of top trails in Raleigh to suit all levels and styles and here is our guide to Umstead State Park.

RAIN IN THE FORECAST?

Don’t despair, if there is rain in the air, there’s plenty of activities in Raleigh this weekend you can do indoors:

  • RALEIGH’S BEST ATTRACTION: We think the free NC Museum of Art is Raleigh’s best foot forward. If the sun peaks out head to their fantastic sculpture park for some outdoor fun!
  • NC’S MOST POPULAR MUSEUM: The free North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences is perfect for a rainy day for all ages. Learn more about the world we live in through fun exhibitions and interactive displays.
  • FOR SPORTS LOVERS: The NC Sports Hall of Fame celebrates excellence in athletics and commemorates and memorializes exceptional accomplishments in sports. It’s located on the third floor of the NC Museum of History (currently closed for renovations). Here is a list of our favorite sports bars in Raleigh, if you want to catch a game with other sports lovers on the weekend!
  • FOR KIDS: You can’t go past Marbles Kids Museum for younger kids. Defy Gravity, Urban Air, and are two fun indoor amusement zones. You also can’t go past the movies, and bowling (check out King’s in North Hills) Here’s a full list of things to do with kids in Raleigh and a list of things to do in Raleigh with teens.
  • WANT MORE? Here are some of Raleigh’s best art galleries and museums and things to do in Raleigh on a rainy day.

LOOKING FOR PLACES TO EAT IN RALEIGH THIS WEEKEND?

  • BRUNCH: It’s the weekend, of course you want a long lingering brunch with peeps you love. Check out these memorable Raleigh brunch spots. Press Coffee & Crepes is our favorite!
  • BREAKFAST: If you want to be more traditional, here are some of our favorite breakfast places in Raleigh.
  • Looking for a date night restaurant? We love Crawford & Son, Second Empire Tavern, Peregrine, Brodeto & Figulina See more date ideas in Raleigh here.
  • LUNCH: Here’s where you can find some of the best sandwiches in Raleigh. And 40+ lunch spots in Raleigh.
  • MORNING COFFEES have never tasted so good at these downtown Raleigh coffee shops, coffee shops worth driving to, and laptop friendly cafes. Don’t miss our very favorite Fount Coffee & Kitchen.
  • DRINKS: Want a view with that cocktail? Try these rooftop bars with a view. We love these Wine Bars in the Raleigh and Raleigh cocktail bars and here are some breweries in Raleigh.
  • BURGERS: We love Burger Village on Glenwood Ave for their gourmet, exotic grass-fed burgers and organic food. More burger joints in Raleigh here.

FEEL LIKE A DAY TRIP?

Who wouldn’t? Vacations don’t always have to involve a plane trip and overnight stay. They can be refreshing adventures just a short car ride away. If you’re looking for getaways from Raleigh this weekend, consider these:

  • JOHNSTON COUNTY: At only 20-40 minutes’ drive away, you’ll find a unique cultural escape in Johnston County. It’s not all farmland fun. There are vineyards, fantastic restaurants, and classy whiskey bars. Check out our date day experience in Joco and a day in Pine Level and Princeton and a day trip from Raleigh to Selma
  • SMALL CITY BREAK: Full of art, culture, food, and local experiences, Durham is always a fun day trip from Raleigh. Here are some ideas on things to do in Durham. We also have ideas on things to do in Chapel Hill. We also love the Pinehurst area! And if you’re going to Greensboro for a concert, we have ideas on other things to do.
  • FOR THE KIDS: They will love learning about birds at Sylvan Heights Bird Park or sliding down waterslides at Wet & Wild or these theme parks near Raleigh
  • BEACH & WATER: Enjoy this day trip to Wrightsville Beach or these other places to swim in Raleigh

And don’t miss our fun day trips from Raleigh.

WHAT ABOUT A FALL GETAWAY?

Fall is a great time to plan a road trip. The mountains are obviously prime leaf peeping territory and beautiful this time of year. As for the coast, the big crowds and heat of summer have left but the temperatures are still pleasant in the 70s. Here are some fall getaway ideas for your planning.

  • Boone is a fantastic getaway and only three hours from Raleigh
  • Roanoke and Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains are also only three hours from Raleigh
  • Everybody loves a visit to Asheville and their outdoor adventures during the fall. Here is our guide to downtown Asheville. Don’t miss the Biltmore Estate, especially their seasonal surprises. We love our stay there at the Biltmore Inn. Here are more places to stay in Asheville.
  • Manteo and Roanoke island is cozy in the Fall and the beach is not too distracting.
  • Head to Danville Virginia for a fun weekend getaway
  • Uplevel your staycation at Umstead Hotel & Spa, Washington Duke Inn & Golf Club, and an hour away at Pinehurst Resort
  • 9 Best getaways from Raleigh in the Fall season
  • Here is a list of day trip ideas from Raleigh

Visiting Raleigh this weekend for an Event?

If you’re visit Raleigh from out of town for any weekly events, here are our recommendations for accommodation in downtown Raleigh.

  • Residence inn Downtown Raleigh – fantastic location and big suites
  • StateView Hotel – hidden away in a forest on NC State’s Campus
  • Casso Hotel – for its uniquely Raleigh boutique feel and AMAZING restaurant (hidden gem!)
  • Best Downtown Raleigh hotels and hotels near Lenovo Center.
  • You may like these upscale hotels near Raleigh including the 5-Star Umstead Hotel & Spa.
  • Check out 10 of our Airbnb rental favorites and see more Raleigh Airbnb rentals here.

If you are visiting from out of town and have a few extra days, here are some itinerary guides to help you plan out your days exploring Raleigh:

  • 24 hour itinerary guide for Raleigh
  • 48-hour itinerary guide for Raleigh NC
  • 2 Day sophisticated itinerary for Raleigh (great with friends)
  • Getting around Raleigh

CLOSING

There you have it, all the cool things to do in Raleigh NC this weekend. Leave us a comment below if you have any events this weekend in Raleigh we should know about? Tell us what you’re doing this weekend in Raleigh? Anything we missed or can include next week for you!
